transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-06-11 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Tom (CTO - Silvermarsh), Mei (Infra Lead), Carlos (Sec Arch), Rina (PM)
---
Summary: Intake to understand Silvermarsh's private onramp and networking constraints. Customer runs analytics platform across EU and APAC, regulatory requirement for EU data at rest + egress controls. Main asks: private endpoint in eu-west-1, Transit Gateway vs peering decision, BYOK/KMS integration, SOC2 artifacts and on-prem egress IPs.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro round, then Priya will drive connectivity questions.
[00:18] Tom: Hi all, Tom here. we're looking at moving inference to a managed runtime, but need a private onramp, can't have data crossing public internet in clear.
[00:27] Priya: Great. can you confirm the primary region you want to start in? iiirc you said EU?
[00:33] Rina: Yes, eu-west-1 for initial pilot. APAC is next quarter.
[00:39] Mei: And we need to ensure avg latency to our app is under 80ms for single-token requests, and we have heavy burst traffic during reports.
[00:48] Jordan: Understood - that shapes batching and instance sizing. also want to surface dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, cost wise.
[00:55] Carlos: Security side: we require SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and we have a corporate policy requiring BYOK via our KMS/HSM. also app logs must not persist in vendor-managed S3 outside EU.
[01:10] Alex: We can provide SOC2 artifacts and support BYOK. we'll share a short security package after this call.
[01:18] Tom: For connectivity, our infra team prefers Transit Gateway because we already use TGW across accounts. but curious about whether Redwood's private endpoints support TGW attachments or do you prefer VPC peering?
[01:31] Priya: Short answer: both are possible. longer answer: for multi-account scale and many spokes, TGW is simpler operationally. our Private offering exposes private endpoints (ENIs/private IPs) in the region VPC that can be routed via TGW. we do ask for route table modifications and specific IP ranges.
[01:49] Mei: when you say private endpoints, is that an AWS PrivateLink-style interface endpoint or something else? and will DNS be split-horizon?
[01:57] Priya: it's similar to PrivateLink - we publish privatelb endpoints in the customer's VPC or in our managed VPC depending on contract. DNS options: we support on-prem DNS override and provide guidance for conditional forwarders so your internal hostnames resolve to private IPs. sometimes the transcript generator writes PrivateLink as private lick, haha
[02:16] (laughter)
[02:20] Tom: Ha, noted. Concerning egress - our security team insists outbound traffic be whitelisted to a small set of IPs and go through our firewall. can your egress be pinned?
[02:30] Jordan: Yes - for Private deployments we can pin egress IPs per region and provide a CIDR list. if you're using Hosted API with VPC onramp, we still can provide static egress via NAT gateways in our managed account or advise using your NAT with routes back to our endpoints.
[02:48] Carlos: We also need to confirm whether logs, prompts, and responses persist in vendor storage; our compliance requires minimal retention and EU-only storage.
[02:58] Alex: We have configurations for zero retention on the hosted path and private can be arranged to store logs in customer-managed S3; we'll note that in the security packet.
[03:08] Rina: For BYOK, we need to do a quick architecture handshake — who manages keys, and do you allow HSM-backed CMKs?
[03:17] Priya: We support customer KMS keys and HSM-backed CMKs. for the Private deployment we can integrate with your KMS for in-flight and at-rest encryption. we'll need KMS ARNs and a short IAM trust policy.
[03:29] Mei: For network topology, our ops lead recommended two options: 1) TGW attachment from our hub into Redwood-managed account, with route tables pointing to the private endpoints; 2) direct VPC peering from our spoke to Redwood VPC. Which has fewer operational pitfalls?
[03:46] Priya: TGW scales better if you have many spokes, fewer peering objects to manage. peering is simpler for one-off connections but can explode if you have dozens. also peering requires careful overlapping CIDR checks. TGW adds a cost but simplifies routing.
[04:00] Tom: Are there any constraints for cross-region requests? we want eu-west-1 for data residency, but Redwood's model infra sometimes runs in other regions for cold-starts.
[04:09] Alex: We pin workloads by model and region per customer. for EU residency we can pin model serving to eu-west-1 and place KV cache locally. we will call out any fallbacks if capacity is constrained; can configure automatic fallback policies that stay within permitted regions.
[04:26] Carlos: Do you provide an audit trail for each inference request and token-level cost breakdown? we need to show examples for auditors.
[04:33] Jordan: Yes - the Console provides token-level cost, per-request tracing hooks, and we can stream audit logs to your customer-managed CloudWatch or S3. we'll include sample traces in the security packet.
[04:44] Mei: On-prem connectivity: we have an on-prem colo that peers via Direct Connect to TGW. latency to eu-west-1 is about 35ms. we plan to keep the control plane out-of-band - are there requirements for the control plane to reach customer IPs?
[04:58] Priya: Control plane stays in our control plane but can be configured with private connectivity for health checks. typically the data plane (inference traffic) moves over the private endpoints. we don't require the control plane to have open inbound ports to on-prem.
[05:10] Tom: For pilot scope, we'd like to run a small workload: 200 concurrent sessions, burst up to 1k rps for report generation across ~20s sequences. what's the recommended deployment? hosted dedicated or private?
[05:25] Jordan: For that pattern, Private in eu-west-1 on a small dedicated pool will give predictable latency and allow you to keep data inside EU. hosted could work if compliance allows and you use private onramp, but dedicated gives capacity guarantees and simpler QoS.
[05:39] Alex: Pricing note - Dedicated/reserved capacity is typically a monthly commit. We'll provide a pilot pricing estimate for a 30-day dedicated pool and an alternative hosted-onramp estimate.
[05:50] Carlos: One more security nuance: our legal team may ask for a subprocessor list and data flow diagram. can you provide those?
[05:58] Alex: Yes, we'll attach subprocessors and a high-level data flow diagram.
[06:03] Rina: On DNS: we need split-horizon so developers hitting internal hostnames resolve to private endpoints. any gotchas?
[06:10] Priya: Make sure conditional forwarders are in place and your internal resolver has entries for the private endpoint hostnames. sometimes customers forget to update resolvers in their EKS nodes; we'll include a short checklist.
[06:21] Tom: About network ranges - we currently use 10.0.0.0/8 in our spokes, vendor VPCs must not overlap. do you accept custom CIDRs?
[06:30] Priya: Yes, we can allocate from a non-overlapping private CIDR for the private endpoint ENIs. we'll request your CIDR ranges and we'll propose a non-conflicting block.
[06:39] Mei: Are TLS mTLS options available between our service and Redwood endpoints? we run mutual TLS internally.
[06:45] Jordan: We support mTLS for private connections; we can share cert rotation guidance.
[06:51] Carlos: Audit retention question - can you stream logs to our S3 in eu-west-1 and ensure log files are encrypted with our KMS?
[06:58] Alex: Yes, we support streaming to customer-managed S3 and encrypt with your KMS. we'll include an example CloudFormation/IaC snippet in the follow-up.
[07:07] Rina: Anything about region peering across clouds? we have some workloads in GCP europe-west4 and in Azure France Central. does Redwood support cross-cloud private endpoints?
[07:18] Priya: Cross-cloud is more nuanced. Our Private runtime can be deployed to multiple cloud regions; private endpoints are per cloud. for GCP/Azure we can provide equivalents (Private Service Connect / Private Link) but it will be separate endpoints and potentially separate configuration. we recommend starting with AWS eu-west-1 then evaluating other clouds.
[07:37] Tom: Ok. next steps? sounds like we need the runbook and the security packet.
[07:42] Alex: Action items captured. we'll send the runbook, SOC2 docs, and a short pilot proposal that outlines the dedicated pool sizing and pricing.
[07:50] Carlos: timeline: we need a legal review window of 2 weeks after receiving docs. pilot ideally next week if we can align infra.
[07:58] Priya: I'll send a connectivity checklist with route table examples and the exact IP/CIDR blocks we ask you to reserve.
[08:05] Mei: I'll pull together our on-prem NAT IPs and forward them to Alex.
[08:11] Tom: thanks everyone, this was great.
[08:15] Alex: Thanks all. we'll follow up with the packet and schedule pilot kickoff.
